abstract: Near-threshold somatosensory stimulation is traditionally applied to investigate the post-stimulus neural correlates of conscious perception as well as ongoing brain activity like alpha oscillations that precede stimulation and modulate perception. Recent findings showed that applying more natural mechanical stimulation instead of the frequently used electric stimulation reveals differences in early post-stimulus perceptual correlates. The precise role of pre-stimulus alpha oscillations requires deeper investigation in the electrical modality and is yet fully undiscovered in the mechanical modality. In this study we investigate post-stimulus neural correlates of conscious perception and shine light on how pre-stimulus alpha amplitude and phase coherence relate to electrical and mechanical stimulus perception. Contrary to previous findings, we found no differences between modalities in early perceptual correlates. Both modalities showed robust correlates of stimulus perception likely corresponding to the N80 and N140 components. The effect of stimulus perception was localised in the right contralateral precentral and postcentral gyri, with the left ipsilateral hemisphere contributing shortly afterwards. We found a negative relationship between the pre-stimulus alpha oscillation amplitude and stimulus perception. Moreover, greater pre-stimulus alpha phase coherence coincided with an increase in stimulus perception. There was no evidence that the alpha effects differed between stimulation modalities.
